Twenty-nine comments

I transcribed this from a compilation CD in a set with another. No title was given for it so I would be pleased if anyone knows it’s name. Last year I submitted two polkas by Lucy Farr. I have made up a set using these in the order: Gan Ainm (here submitted); Lucy Farr’s no 2 (Nov 25th 2004); Lucy Farr’s no1 (Nov 24th 2004).

↳ Posted by ceolachan on December 4th, 2005.

Hi ‘c’. had not considered this in respect to being related to Tralee Goal, or for that matter ‘Glen Cottage’, which I have also started playing recently.
I already play a version of ‘Tralee’ within a set which I call ‘Fish & Taters’. I contributed that to the session some time ago. I have no details on the source of that set as it was taught to me a very long time ago by a mandoline player and I learnt it on whistle.
Interestingly & recently Johnny O‘Leary’s was contributed to the session as a slide, but it was more familiar to me as a polka and I was aware of it’s closeness to ’Tralee’.
This tune however has much which makes it sufficiently different so I hope it stands as a contribution and hope Jeremy does not remove it but we shall have to wait and see.

↳ Posted by hetty on December 5th, 2005.

So! what do I call it??

↳ Posted by hetty on December 5th, 2005.

“The Glen Cottage Polka #2”

It is the 2nd of the set known as “The Glen Cottage Polkas”… While it shares the same first part with all the others the second part is basically a variant of the other second parts, but as you said, sufficiently different in a few places… In you version, with very little difference aside from basic variations, it exists under this name in several existing collections…

↳ Posted by ceolachan on December 5th, 2005.

“The Glen / Glin / Green Cottage Polka 2 / 3”

“Johnny O’Leary of Sliabh Luachra”
Edited by Terry Moylan
The Lilliput Press, 1994
ISBN: 1-874675-42-2

Page 137-138 ~ Tune #237: “The Glin Cottage Polka”
( “Glin Cottage Polkas 2” )
Again the same tune though Johnny has some different ways at times with it…for example, with the first bar, he may play it |: eA Bd| ~ or ~ |: ef/e/ Bd | ~ or ~

“Mally Presents 100 Irish Polkas”
Edited by Dave Mallinson
Dave Mallinson Publications, 1997
ISBN: 1-899512-21-7

Page 1 ~ Tune #2: “The Glen Cottage No.2”
Again identical except A Dorian instead of E Dorian and the usual variations.

“110 Ireland’s Best Polkas & Slides”
Waltons Music Inc., 1999
ISBN: 1-85720-086-1

Page 22 ~ Tune # 49: “The Glen Cottage Polka (2)”
Identical except for key, A Dorian, and the usual polka variations…

“Matt Cunningham’s Dance Music of Ireland”
Dave Mallinson Publications, 1999
ISBN: 1-899512-45-4

Page 33: “The Green Cottage Polka No.3”
Again in A Dorian and the same tune…

By ‘usual variations’ I mean, using the first two bars as an example, just four, starting with the least, in this case in both keys of A & E Dorian:

A-Part ~ B-Part

|: BE FA | B>A FA | ~ |: B2 cd | eB cB |

|: BE E/F/A | BA F/G/A | ~ |: B>A B/c/d | eB c/B/A |

|: e2 A/B/c/d/ | ed Bd | ~ |: e/f/e/d/ e2 | ae f/e/d/B/ |
